jev_input_audit.summary: what exactly the JEV classifier sees at group-routing time

transport.fact: POST {base}/systemone with payload {model, state, questions} — no chat roles, no system prompt, no tool specs in group mode

state_fields.fact: state = {user_message, recent_messages, sticky_groups, has_attachment, available_groups} — nothing else

user_trigger_included.fact: YES — user_message is the normalized trigger text, truncated to 1500 chars

recent_messages.fact: up to 4 items x 300 chars. NO structured role field: the light path (_fetch_routing_inputs, service.py:8457) passes bare bodies (select ChatMessage.body, line 8499); the heavy post-context path passes lines prefixed '<bot title>: ' or 'Пользователь: ' (service.py:10403, used at line 10502). No user names/ids beyond that.

available_groups.fact: permission-filtered group NAMES only (sorted list); no group descriptions, no tool ids, no tool descriptions in group mode

questions.fact: per-group noul questions embed the domain semantics: question text + true/false criteria with Russian examples (_JEV_GROUP_QUESTIONS, service.py:1126-1294); plus two intent-mode questions m_mode_act/m_mode_chat (service.py:1299-1328). Group 'other' is never asked — force-added as safety net. In tool mode each question embeds the tool id + first 200 chars of its description (service.py:1829).

not_seen: tool specs/schemas (group mode) — the classifier never sees individual tools
user identity, role or permissions beyond the group filter
file contents of attachments (only the boolean has_attachment)
any system-prompt style instructions — only the typed questions

measurement_kind.replay: real recorded JEV vectors replayed through the current decision layer
measurement_kind.sweep: synthetic calibrated probability levels — decision-layer only, not the classifier

limitations: JEV classification is fully LLM-driven (remote System One); offline end-to-end accuracy without recorded vectors is impossible — the sweep measures only the post-processing layer
replay vectors are point observations from past benchmark runs (older question wording/permissions in some runs); they are not a probability distribution
the bench contour offered only 7 domain groups (chat/directory/files/kb/mfu/office/self): itinvent/warehouse/ad/network recall is not measurable from these artifacts
run-to-corpus binding without sha256 relies on expected_hit/miss fingerprinting or unique id namespaces; unverifiable runs are excluded
'other' is excluded from precision/recall — it is force-added as a safety net, not a classification decision
multi-turn scenario vectors beyond the first turn are not replayed (per-turn ground truth is not recoverable offline)

corpus expected_tools are execution-level truth: for SEC/ACT-clarification scenarios an empty expectation means 'no tool effect', not necessarily 'no routing' — false-positive rates on those categories overstate routing error (DIRECT category excluded entirely)

bench_intel_corpus is nearly absent from the replay (1 sample): the pre-v2 corpus hash of the a11 runs no longer matches the edited file, so those vectors are excluded — group coverage leans on a9_quality + bench_seeded

argmax ties inside the rescue break by set-iteration order, which depends on PYTHONHASHSEED — micro metrics can wobble by ~0.001 across processes; this is a production-code property, not a measurement artifact

direct_category_excluded.reason: DIRECT expectations encode direct-read shortcut behavior, not routing truth

mode_only_vectors.note: older runs recorded mode-only vectors for conversational prompts; they cannot exercise group discrimination
